command:
backlog task create "ambient-bleed asserts a fact it never checked: approval env marks its own exports so the documented start ritual stops being reported as cross-instance bleed" --type bug --priority Medium -s "In Progress" -a @opus-278 --desc "\`findingsFor\` in src/core/instance.ts emits kind \`ambient-bleed\` for every resolved variable whose status is \`set-in-environment\` when the instance's env file also carries a line for it, with the detail \"...is exported in this environment, so <home>'s own line N was not consulted: the value in use is not the one this instance configured\".

The rule reads no values by design (APRV-178, NON_RESOLVING_RUNNER) and so cannot tell a FOREIGN export from the one \`eval \\\"\\\$(approval env)\\\"\` just made from THIS instance's own file. That eval is the documented start ritual (docs/dogfood-cutover.md, \`approval up\`'s own preflight text), so the finding fires on the correct path and asserts something the rule never checked.

Observed 2026-09-06 in the primary: \`unset APPROVAL_SAMPLING_SECRET && eval \\\"\\\$(approval env)\\\" && approval up\` printed the finding for that variable. \`approval up\` prints it on stderr at start; \`approval doctor\`'s keychain-scope row has the same source.

Fix: have \`approval env\` mark what it exported, without values. The export block emits one extra provenance variable naming the format version, the instance id, the sha256 of the env file bytes it resolved from, and the names it exported from that file. \`findingsFor\` then treats a \`set-in-environment\` variable as this instance's own export when the provenance variable is present, current, and names it, and emits no finding. Anything else still produces the finding, with wording narrowed to what was actually verified.

Invariant 7 (no verb loads the working-tree file implicitly) and the no-values rule both hold: the provenance variable carries an id, a digest and NAMES, never a value, and only a human evaluating \`approval env\` puts it into a shell." --ac "The documented ritual is quiet: with the instance's own \`approval env\` export block evaluated in the shell, findingsFor emits NO ambient-bleed finding for a variable that block exported from this instance's env file" --ac "A foreign export (a value exported with no provenance variable present) still produces an ambient-bleed finding, worded only as what was verified: exported before this process started, not this instance's own \`approval env\` export, and the file's line N not consulted" --ac "Provenance naming ANOTHER instance's id produces the finding" --ac "Provenance whose env-file digest does not match the file as it now reads produces the finding" --ac "\`approval env\`'s export block emits the provenance variable, it carries no value on any path, and it lists only names resolved from the file (never a value passed through from the ambient environment)" --ac "The provenance variable's shape is documented in \`approval env --help\` and in docs/cli-reference.md \`## env\`" --ac "NON_RESOLVING_RUNNER semantics are unchanged: no keystore is consulted to compute a finding" --plain 2>&1 | tail -20
